title: Smooth morphisms are locally standard smooth
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $x\in X$. Then there are affine open subschemes $V\subseteq S$ and $W\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $x\in W$ and $f(W)\subseteq V$ such that, with $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$, $A=\mathcal O_X(W)$ and $\varphi:R\to A$ the ring map induced by $f$ (the composite of $f^\sharp_V:\mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V))$ with the restriction $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V))\to\mathcal O_X(W)$), the $R$-algebra $A$ is standard smooth [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01V7 (label lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth, line 7191; proof: 'Follows from the definitions and Algebra, Lemmas 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth) and 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic)'), applied with any affine open V containing f(x); smoothness in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is that of Morphisms Definition 01V5 by more-morphisms.tex Lemma 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth)
